items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy Lunceford was the main man. He was the leader... But all of them had to just take their hats off to Sy Oliver... They didn't play the way it hit with him... any of them in that band.

ctx.x: How did you all get the kind of discipline that it took for that kind of cleanness to come out of the band?
Well, Jimmy Lunceford was the main man. He was the leader, he was the teacher of discipline and

whatnot. But I have to give credit where it's due. That Sy Oliver got in there and Willie Smith, yes, he arranged. But all of them had to just take their hats off to Sy Oliver. Sy Melvin Oliver never (inaudible). That man, he really was the instigator of all the precision work and just played his arrangements. And he'd get pretty burned up, too, at times. If you didn't do it right. But Willie Smith, without a doubt, would get very horrified with any saxophone player there -- Jack Carruthers, Joe Thomas, Willie…
